audit_findings.title: Recurring currency-conversion costs may have been stripped from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.9 million in FY2025 and $15.1 million in the nine months ended May 31, 2026; FY2025 amount equals 9.8% of the $151.3 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring conversion costs must remain deducted in historical and projected OE; adding them back raises the OE anchor and every discounted cash-flow period.
audit_findings.evidence: For the twelve months ended August 31, 2025, the primary drivers of Other expense, net were $14.9 million of transaction costs, associated with converting the local currencies into available tradable currencies before converting them to U.S. dollars in some of our countries with foreign exchange liquidity issues.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that these are recurring cash transaction costs, including a nine-month FY2026 amount already exceeding FY2025's annual amount. The unresolved issue is whether the OE calculations stripped them with other foreign-currency items. At nearly 10% of anchor OE before tax effects, an erroneous add-back could materially change intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Audit every annual OE reconciliation, separate conversion transaction costs from noncash remeasurement gains or losses, and rerun all scenarios with recurring conversion costs deducted.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may value trapped foreign cash as freely distributable cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.1 million of Trinidad-dollar cash and investments at May 31, 2026 within the $322.191 million cash/STI bridge; required haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A haircut for conversion premiums, devaluation, operating minimums, restrictions, or repatriation taxes reduces the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: However, as the Trinidad central bank strictly manages the exchange rate of the Trinidad dollar with the U.S. dollar and affects the level of U.S. dollar liquidity in the market through its interventions, we are subject to continued challenges in converting our Trinidad dollars to U.S. dollars, as well as being exposed to the risk of a potential devaluation of the currency.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates continuing Trinidad conversion constraints and identifies $44.1 million exposed there, but it does not provide the country-level composition, operating requirements, taxes, or realizable USD value of the full bridge balance. The identified Trinidad balance is 13.7% of bridge cash but only 1.8% of the $2.448 billion base equity value; broader foreign-cash restrictions could increase the effect, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the May 31, 2026 cash and investment balances by country, currency, restriction and operating requirement; quantify conversion and repatriation costs; then rerun the bridge using distributable USD-equivalent cash.

audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings omit the incoming CEO's recurring compensation
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.0 million annual pretax compensation, equal to 3.3% of the $151.3 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalizing recurring CEO compensation lowers sustainable OE and therefore operating value; it does not affect shares or the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For fiscal year 2026, we estimate that general and administrative expenses will be impacted by $5.0 million for the compensation of our Chief Executive Officer.
audit_findings.explanation: FY2025 demonstrably lacked CEO compensation, while the company expected $5.0 million annually and reported that FY2026 G&A includes the new CEO's compensation. No normalization is visible in the supplied anchor. The gross expense is only 3.3% of anchor OE before any tax benefit, too small to change the valuation conclusion given the $77.41 base value versus the $174.10 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the precise CEO and payroll-related amount embedded in FY2026 results and rerun the OE anchor and scenarios with a normalized recurring charge.

audit_findings.title: Recurring tax advances and disputed receivables are not visibly reconciled to owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $96.065 million of VAT and income-tax receivables at May 31, 2026, including $53.139 million classified as noncurrent; recurring cash drag unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring compulsory tax advances reduce OE through working-capital investment, while separately recoverable accumulated receivables could increase the equity bridge if not already captured; recognizing both would double count.
audit_findings.evidence: This collection mechanism generally leaves us with net VAT and/or income tax receivables, forcing us to process significant refund claims on a recurring basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate material balances, multiyear recovery periods and recurring advance-payment mechanisms, but they do not isolate the sustainable annual cash drag. The $96.065 million recorded asset equals 3.9% of the $2.448 billion base equity value, while the potentially capitalized value of a recurring drag is unquantified. Direction is mixed because OE may be overstated while the cash-only bridge may omit a recoverable asset.
audit_findings.action: Build a jurisdiction-level roll-forward of cash taxes, VAT collections, refunds, offsets and write-offs; estimate normalized annual investment and recovery timing; then rerun either OE or the bridge without double counting.

audit_findings.title: An uncommenced long-term lease may create future occupancy cost absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.114 million of filed future fixed lease payments for the Miraflores relocation, equal to 1.1% of the $2.448 billion base equity value; incremental rent unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Only incremental rent above the existing location's occupancy expense should reduce projected OE when the replacement lease commences; the lease should not also be deducted as debt if rent is included in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of August 31, 2025, the Company has signed a lease agreement for a facility to be built by the lessor related to the relocation of its warehouse club in Miraflores, Guatemala.
audit_findings.explanation: The May 2026 filing confirms that the Miraflores lease had not commenced, so its new rent is absent from the historical anchor and recognized operating-lease liabilities. However, the entire filed fixed-payment stream is only 1.1% of base equity value before recognizing that existing-location rent is already expensed and only the incremental difference matters. This is not large enough on the supplied scale to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the new and old lease schedules, commencement date, CPI terms and expected variable rent; calculate incremental occupancy expense and include it in projected OE without deducting the same lease liability in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit obligations are claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.745 million of post-employment-plan liabilities reported within other long-term liabilities at May 31, 2026, equal to 0.6% of the $2.448 billion base equity value or $0.47 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any net underfunded obligation for past service not already represented by projected benefit expense should be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company's subsidiaries located in three countries have unfunded post-employment benefit plans (defined benefit plans) in which the subsidiary is required to pay a specified benefit upon retirement, voluntary departure or death of the employee.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is a demonstrated senior claim, but even the gross May 2026 amount—before offsetting any plan-related restricted funds—is only 0.6% of base equity value and approximately $0.47 per diluted share. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile current and long-term plan liabilities to restricted plan funds and projected OE benefit payments, then deduct only the net past-service obligation not already captured in future OE.
